actual_checks: Full exact report, literal prompt, provenance/source records and full prior product-Kummer/section-propagation manuscript read. The regime all geometric Picard ranks >=5 plus explicit quartic certificate is distinct from the earlier elementary positive-section case, though the broad elliptic density theorem is correctly already credited there.

In characteristic zero the geometric Neron–Severi lattice has signature (1,rho-1); Meyer indefinite-rank-at-least-five theorem gives a nonzero rational isotropic vector and clearing denominators an integral square-zero class. Schutt–Shioda Proposition 12.8 supplies the reflection/linear-system passage to a genus-one fibration, not necessarily with a section. Its characteristic 2/3 quasi-elliptic disclaimer does not apply here.

A single fixed fibration has finitely many algebraic coefficients and descends to one finite number-field extension; Bogomolov–Tschinkel Theorem 1.1 then supplies potential density over a further single finite extension. No positive Mordell–Weil rank section, arbitrary infinite field compositum or uniform degree bound is substituted.

For a smooth quartic, adjunction gives line self-intersection -2, hyperplane square 4 and hyperplane-line degree 1; four disjoint lines give determinant (-2)^4(4+2)=96 and five independent geometric divisor classes. The Fermat quartic is smooth in characteristic zero, and its four lines x0=a_i x1,x2=a_i x3, a_i^4=-1, lie on it and are pairwise skew by direct coordinate comparison. Lines need not be rational over K.

Rank-four even form 2(7t^2-x^2-y^2-z^2) is anisotropic: t=0 forces zero, even t gives all-even coordinates modulo 4 and descent, and odd t gives impossible three-square residue 7 modulo 8. This only demonstrates failure of Meyer in rank four; neither lattice realization on a K3 nor a counterexample to potential density is asserted.
